newsitem.title: INDIA: Bhutto says voters rejected hawkish stand on India.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto says voters rejected hawkish stand on India.

text.p: Pakistans ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto said on Sunday the countrys voters had rejected her hawkish policy on India and Kashmir and backed her successors stand on reopening bilateral talks.

"I must say Nawaz Sharif made no secret of his policy to improve relations with India. We had a more hawkish policy on India," Bhutto told Asian News International television in an interview conducted in the Pakistani city of Karachi.

"He (Sharif) is the one with a three-fourths majority so obviously the people have endorsed his stand to open negotiations with India and they have rejected our stand that unless India moves on the Kashmir issue there would be no talks," Bhutto said.
Over a dozen militant groups are fighting for
independence or merger of Kashmir with neighbouring Pakistan. Jammu and Kashmir is mainly Hindu India's only majority state.

More than 20,000 people have been killed since 1990 when discontent against Indian rule erupted into revolt. India accuses Pakistan of training and arming Kashmir's Moslem militants, a charge denied by Islamabad.
Sharif is due to be sworn in as prime minister on Monday to take over from caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid. He has yet to spell out his governments ideas .
Pakistan said on Friday that Deve Gowdas offer for talks was pointless unless the subject of Kashmir was on the table.
On Friday India said it favoured strengthening economic ties with Pakistan and would soon take steps to promote business travel between the two longtime enemies.

In the television interview Bhutto repeated charges that this months national election was rigged. On Saturday Pakistans Election Commission rejected claims by members of her party that the army had joined in alleged rigging.
"I think there has been massive bungling in the elections," Bhutto said in the interview, but added:

"However, I think that if we have a prime minister who has a majority then we should give him a chance to rid our present system of its ills...The prime minister had become helpless in Pakistan. The army, president and the intelligence agencies, everybody used to bully him and push him."
"As a (former) prime minister I am happy that the new prime minister has a chance to define the powers of the chief executive and to make the parliament the heart of politics."
